# Case study 1: Sourcing niche mentorship & wrap-around support

Status: **scoped — API call identified, ready for someone with backend access to run**

## Scope (decided 2026-07-24)

Standing, general scenario — not tied to a specific event. Persona: an early-career
researcher (ECR/trainee), at any point in time, whose local institution lacks mentorship
in a specific skill or standard they need. The All-Hands lightning-pitch matching (see
`notes/context.md`) is precedent/evidence that this is workable, not the scope itself.

**Validation approach**: manual expert review of shortlists generated from synthetic
personas (no real-person consent needed for a first pass) — Moni/Vikram/Janani judge
relevance once Zhandos or Jiawei runs the queries below through ORCID-authenticated
access.

## Synthetic test personas

Each is deliberately cross-DGP / cross-institution-type, since "niche" mentorship is
precisely the case where the right mentor is unlikely to be at the same institution or
in the same DGP.

**Persona A — wet-lab-to-ML gap.**
Postdoc, CM4AI, wet-lab genomics/proteomics background, first time needing to apply
ML/AI-readiness standards (e.g., FAIRSCAPE-style data packaging) to her own data. Non-R1
institution. Needs: a mentor who has *actually done* AI-readiness standardization on
biological data, not just a computational person in general.

**Persona B — clinical-to-governance gap.**
Clinical fellow, CHoRUS or AI-READi, strong clinical/EHR data background, PI is asking
them to help draft a data governance / responsible-AI section of a paper or protocol.
Healthcare/clinical institution type. Needs: a mentor with ELSI/data-governance
publication history, ideally with prior Bridge2AI-standards authorship (the 54-paper set
in `notes/context.md` is a natural candidate pool).

**Persona C — grant-writing-translation gap.**
Early-career data scientist, Voice DGP, technically strong, has never co-written an
interdisciplinary grant with a clinical partner. Needs: a mentor who has bridged
clinical + technical co-authorship across institutions before (i.e., has demonstrable
cross-institution, cross-DGP collaboration in their own publication history) — someone
who can teach the *process*, not just supply domain content.

## KG query spec (for Zhandos/Jiawei to execute)

**Exact path, confirmed from `cm4ai-bot`'s README** (2026-07-27): since none of the three
synthetic personas is an actual KG node, the right entry point is the same one the app
uses for newly-onboarded authors, not the node-click "Find Teaming Opportunities" UI
flow (that one requires an existing `aid`):

```
POST /api/author-preview
Body: { full_name, affiliation, papers: [{ title, journal?, year?, doi?, url? }], top_k? }
```

- Backend batch-encodes the `papers` titles with SPECTER2, takes the mean vector as the
  persona's embedding, and runs it against the FAISS index — same mechanism the app uses
  to place a real newly-added author on the atlas.
- For each persona, `papers` should be a handful of representative title-like strings
  standing in for their stated expertise + gap (there's no free-text "describe yourself"
  field — it only accepts a papers list, so the persona's expertise needs to be encoded
  as invented-but-plausible paper titles, e.g. "FAIRSCAPE-style data packaging for
  proteomics" for Persona A).
- Response: de-duplicated nearest static author ids with a normalized similarity score
  and name/affiliation metadata — no topic/expertise labels are surfaced (confirms no
  curated affinity-tag layer exists yet, per `notes/context.md`).
- Record, per candidate: name, institution, similarity score. DGP affiliation and PI flag
  are **not** in this response — those would need a manual second lookup against
  `author_metadata.json`/the admin catalog per candidate id.

**Cross-institution/DGP exclusion — confirmed NOT supported.** The only built-in
exclusion is *already-known collaborators*, via `GET /api/collaborators/{aid}` — and
that only works for an existing `aid`, which none of these synthetic personas have. So
for `/api/author-preview` there is no automatic exclusion of any kind; institution/DGP
diversity in the results is not enforced and must be filtered manually after the fact by
the reviewer.

**Onboarding-data / mentorship-history bias — confirmed NOT wired in.** The
recommendation is pure SPECTER2-embedding similarity over paper titles; there is no
signal in `cm4ai-bot` for "has mentored before," career stage, or anything from
`b2ai_survey`'s onboarding data. If we want that, it has to happen as a manual
post-filter step on our side (join returned candidate names/affiliations against
`career_stage_simple` from `b2ai_data`), not something to ask Zhandos/Jiawei to change
in the pipeline for this case study.

Cap each shortlist at ~10 candidates (`top_k=10`) for review.

## Expected output

A shortlist per persona: ranked candidates (name, affiliation, similarity score) from
`/api/author-preview`, with DGP/PI-flag looked up manually per candidate, and
institution/DGP diversity checked manually since there's no native filter for it. No
topic-overlap explanation is returned by the API — if reviewers want to sanity-check
*why* a candidate matched, that means separately checking the candidate's bibliography
for topical overlap with the invented persona papers.

## Validation rubric (manual review, once shortlists exist)

For each candidate, reviewer (Moni/Vikram/Janani) rates 1–5:
- **Topical relevance** — does the shared-topic evidence actually match the stated gap?
- **Seniority appropriateness** — plausibly more senior/experienced in the gap area?
- **Cross-boundary value** — different institution/DGP from the persona (the point of
  "niche" sourcing is reaching outside the persona's existing network)?
- **Actionability** — would a human matchmaker actually suggest this pairing without
  more information?

A case study is "validated" if ≥2 of 3 reviewers rate ≥2 of the top-5 candidates per
persona at 4+ on all four axes. (Threshold is a starting proposal — revisit once we see
real output; may be too strict or too loose.)

## Non-KG-member trainees (AIM-AHEAD, etc.)

Confirmed workable per the All-Hands precedent: use their stated pitch/topic text as a
direct query input without requiring a pre-existing KG node. Worth adding as an explicit
4th persona (non-member trainee) once the three above are validated, to confirm the same
mechanism holds outside the event context.

## Data dependency

Needs role/career-stage data from `b2ai_survey` onboarding data
(`career_stage_simple`, `institution_type`) to distinguish "junior seeking mentor" from
"senior offering mentorship" at scale beyond these 3 hand-built personas — this is the
7/22 action item Janani owes, and becomes more valuable once this case study is
validated (to generalize past hand-picked personas).
